articles.headline: EU cyber law triggers urgent 24-hour vulnerability reporting for connected products
articles.summary: The EU’s Cyber Resilience Act reporting obligations began on 11 September, requiring manufacturers of connected products sold in Europe to report actively exploited vulnerabilities within 24 hours. For businesses, this raises compliance costs, accelerates incident-response timelines, and increases exposure to heavy penalties if reporting workflows are not already in place.

articles.headline: U.S. regulators open antitrust probe into Nvidia’s Groq deal structure
articles.summary: U.S. authorities are investigating whether Nvidia structured its roughly $20 billion licensing arrangement with Groq to avoid antitrust review. The case matters to chip buyers, suppliers, and investors because it could reshape AI infrastructure deal-making and add regulatory risk to major semiconductor transactions.

articles.headline: Oracle cloud revenue surges on AI demand, beating Wall Street estimates
articles.summary: Oracle reported quarterly cloud infrastructure revenue up 121% to $7.4 billion, above analyst expectations, driven by AI demand. For businesses, the result signals continued pressure on cloud capacity and pricing dynamics as enterprises expand AI workloads.
